# The metrics they chose

Sweeps 1 and 2 asked eight synthetic athletes for data in the developer's
categories - steps, sleep, calories, heart rate. Sweep 3 asked a different
question: **what do YOU want counted?**

Almost none of it fits the schema. This file is the raw inventory, kept as
evidence for G78-G84. Several of these are things the athlete has counted
privately for years and never written anywhere.

## The inventory

### Counters and tallies
- times I said yes instead of "you go on, I'll wait here"
- times I got outside with him, even just to the postbox and back
- mornings I got out the door before the house woke up
- weeks I didn't drop a planned session even though the week was a write-off
- how many times a week I put real clothes on rather than the same leggings
- evenings I actually cooked rather than ate standing up out of a container
- times I opened the reunion event page and closed it again without doing anything
- how many evenings I go an hour without checking my phone for no reason
- sessions finished completely alone, nobody at the finish
- **sessions I skipped on purpose, guilt-free, with no makeup session added later**

### Days-since (reset on the event)
- days since a bad knee day tipped into a bad mood day
- days since we had a proper meal together rather than crossing in the kitchen
- days since I had a proper laugh - "not a smirk at the telly, an actual laugh"
- days since a genuinely bad night - "reset to zero every time, like a
  superstition. I want to watch that number try to climb past three, because it
  never has"
- weeks since a session felt EASY rather than merely completed
- nights since I slept longer than four hours straight ("it's six, I know it
  without checking")
- months since anyone last called me "big Rachel" to my face
- **years since Dad died at sixty-one** ("I count that one whether I want to or
  not, every birthday it ticks over")
- months until the custody arrangement ends and my youngest turns eighteen

### Reset-on-fail streaks
- nights in a row without eating from the vending machine at 3am - "resets to
  zero the second a Twix happens"
- Fridays in a row with two pints instead of four

### Fractions and pass/fail against a named obstacle
- **"12 of 14"** - stairs climbed at home without stopping, out of the flight he
  built the bannister for twenty years ago
- the stairs to the third-floor flat with both shopping bags, in one go, without
  putting them down "and pretending to check my phone"
- the stairs with the pram without stopping halfway
- did I take the stairs at school rather than getting the lift excuse ready

### Non-scale body anchors
- **belt holes**, measured against a wedding-day belt kept in a drawer for
  fifteen years - "that's my actual scale, more than any number on the bathroom
  one"

### Occupational capacity
- fares in a row before needing to sit in the cab for ten minutes
- finished a job at work without needing a breather I did not used to need

### Relational (the dyad is the subject)
- did we sit down together of an evening, not just in the same room with the telly
- conversations with my partner where neither of us has a phone in hand
- whether we walked together - "not the distance, not the calories. Whether we did it"
- whether the kids came and watched, **and which one** - the two of them watching
  are two different things
- did I read to him, even for two minutes

### Affective and self-perception
- did a session feel easy - "not RPE. RPE tells you how hard. This is whether it
  felt light and joyful at any point"
- whether I looked forward to a shift versus just survived it ("running about
  30/70 lately, and that bothers me more than my weight ever has")
- times I caught myself in a shop window or a photo and didn't immediately look away
- did the on-week feel like time with them, or like a countdown to them leaving
- good day / bad day "in myself" - "some days I feel like a man of 53 and some
  days I feel like an old fella, and it's not always the same day as the good numbers"
- evenings I wasn't the last one still at the table, picking at nothing

### Ritual and superstition
- **magpies on the path before 7am** - "if I see three before the bridge it's
  going to be a good session, one is a bad omen. I have genuinely turned around
  threshold sessions in my head based on magpie count. I would never say this to
  my old coach."
- a private head-to-head with a friend on three local segments - "I would never
  admit to him that I know the score. I know the score."

### Explicitly private (hidden from the coach)
- nights without the heavy chest feeling after eating too much too late - "I'd
  want it private, not something that shows up on a screen anyone else sees"
- the magpie count, the segment ledger, the custody countdown, the "big Rachel"
  count

### Explicitly refused - known, kept, and not to be recorded
- a running count of bad shifts, meaning ones where a patient died - "I've never
  told anyone that number exists... some of it isn't for tracking."

## What this inventory proves

1. **Most are not measurements.** They are counters, days-since, streaks,
   fractions and binaries. The quantity apparatus (anchor / measured-flow /
   modeled-estimate, rates, trends) fits almost none of them. -> G79
2. **Magnitude is frequently excluded on purpose.** "Five useless minutes counts
   the same as the full session." Quantifying would destroy the thing being
   measured. -> G79
3. **Six of eight named a relational metric** unprompted. -> G80
4. **Privacy is per-metric, and sometimes the answer is do not store it at all.**
   -> G81
5. **Not one of the eight named a number** when asked what they would be sad to
   lose in five years. -> G83
